The '''GR-45 medium transport''' was a type of cargo [[Transport/Legends|transport]] manufactured by [[Gallofree Yards, Inc./Legends|Gallofree Yards, Inc.]], and shared similarities with the company's [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]].

==Characteristics==
The GR-45 [[Transport/Legends|medium transport]] was similar in design and appearance to the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] also produced by [[Gallofree Yards, Inc./Legends|Gallofree Yards]], which saw use by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. Unlike the GR-75, the GR-45 was intended for civilian use, and contained a large cargo space that could be filled by teams of [[ASP-7 labor droid/Legends|ASP-7 labor droids]].<ref name="ITW" />

==History==
A dilapidated GR-45 was parked illegally on [[Outer Curved Street/Legends|Outer Curved Street]] in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]<ref name="ITW" /> at the time of the arrival of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], and their [[Droid/Legends|droids]], to the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] [[City/Legends|city]]. Teams of [[ASP-7 labor droid/Legends|ASP-7 labor droids]] were loading the vessel as Kenobi and Skywalker passed by in an [[X-34 landspeeder/Legends|X-34 landspeeder]], seeking a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] to [[Transport/Legends|transport]] them to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The ASPs were scheduled to have the GR-45's cargo-space loaded by suns-set.<ref name="ITW" />

==Behind the scenes==
The GR-45 medium transport first appeared in scenes included in the [[1997]] Special Edition re-release of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], although it was not named until the [[2004]] reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]'' by [[Dorling Kindersley]].
